items.title: Show HN :Tandem – one session across Claude Code and Codex, no double spend
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shipped Tandem, a tool that syncs your active coding sessions across Claude Code and Codex so you don't double-spend on LLM tokens. Since you use both of these tools daily, this directly solves the context-switching tax and keeps your API costs down. You can clone the repository today and run it locally to sync your active AI-ingest workspace across both environments.

items.title: Show HN: Dissecting the automation of a newspaper (Claude routine, GitHub Pages)
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shipped a fully automated daily newspaper built with Claude and GitHub Pages that costs just $0.55 per edition to run, sharing the entire open-source codebase. It is a prime example of a solo builder shipping a creative, low-cost project using the same AI-directed approach you are learning. You can clone his repository this week to study how he structures his automated Claude prompts and deploys the static output.

items.title: Show HN: PinFix – Click any UI element and edit its source with Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: PinFix is a new open-source utility that lets you click on any UI element in your browser and immediately edit its source code using Claude Code. This removes the friction of hunting down Next.js component files when you want to make quick visual changes. You can install it on your local AI-ingest project today to speed up your frontend tweaks.

items.title: Show HN: Shellphone, an MCP Extension to Link Claude Chat and Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: Shellphone is a new MCP extension that links your browser-based Claude Chat with your terminal-based Claude Code. This lets you seamlessly pass context and commands between the two interfaces without manual copying and pasting. You can install this npm package this week to bridge your web research sessions directly into your active coding terminal.
